claim: Let \(K=T_{7,1,2}\) be the Datta--Upadhyay seven-vertex torus on \(\mathbb Z/7\mathbb Z\), with faces \(\{i,i+2,i+3\}\) and \(\{i,i+1,i+3\}\). For every vertex set \(S\subseteq V(K)\), let \(r(S)\) be the \(\mathbf F_2\)-rank of the image of \(H_1(K[S];\mathbf F_2)\to H_1(K;\mathbf F_2)\). Then the complete rank distribution by \(|S|\) is: ranks \(0\) on the unique empty set; rank \(0\) on all \(7\) one-sets and all \(21\) two-sets; on three-sets, rank \(0\) for the \(14\) faces and rank \(1\) for the \(21\) empty triangles; on four-sets, rank \(1\) for \(21\) sets and rank \(2\) for \(14\) sets, with \(r(S)=2\) exactly when the complementary three-set is a face; and every five-, six-, or seven-vertex set has rank \(2\). Moreover, the \(21\) empty triangles represent the three nonzero classes of \(H_1(K;\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^2\) exactly seven times each. Consequently, five is the least integer \(k\) such that every \(k\)-vertex induced subcomplex surjects onto \(H_1(K;\mathbf F_2)\).
integrity: All finite cases in the claim are exhaustively checked by exact binary linear algebra from the published face formula; search absence is not treated as proof of novelty.
scientific_limitations: The classification is over \(\mathbf F_2\) only and is specific to the unique seven-vertex torus; no integral-class or larger-triangulation statement is made.
title: A sharp five-vertex homology-support threshold for the seven-vertex torus
